source.scope: Fleet replay, the sole product demo; the former single-vessel comparison is retired.
source.method: Code extraction from the final cascade and current component markup. No new visual review or application tests were run for this documentation handoff.

finalCascadeNotes: Introduction is block layout, overriding the earlier two-column declaration.
Final reading-size overrides raise report text and chart footnotes.
Final narrow vessel facts use two columns, overriding an earlier four-column rule.
Map labels remain 150px wide at every breakpoint.
Map legend sits 38px from the bottom, or 34px at 650px and below.

observed: 3px teal focus-visible outline with 4px offset on buttons, links, inputs, selects, and summaries.
Focus-revealed skip link to fleet replay.
Semantic tablist with roving tabindex and ArrowLeft, ArrowRight, Home, and End navigation.
aria-pressed for vessel selection and condition presets.
Native range, select, checkbox, details, summary, and semantic data tables.
Accessible names for icon controls; inline decorative SVG uses aria-hidden.
Loading/frame/response status regions and service-error alert region.
Coordinate fallback has a descriptive accessible label and keyboard-selectable vessel groups.
limits: This extraction is not a complete accessibility audit.
The inspect-vessel JavaScript action explicitly requests smooth scrolling even under reduced motion.
Small contextual labels remain in the implementation; do not interpret the type scale as a general minimum target-size or contrast certification.

modelTabs: C The Antidote; only C shows the response banner
response: review; provisional human check with changed title, copy, color and SVG
controls: disabled while unavailable; half opacity and wait cursor
facts: historical error marked as retrospective scoring
known simulated changes marked for audience only

researchIntegrity.purpose: Visual states and snippets must preserve source truth.
constraints: Use actual fitted-model outputs; controls do not retrain models.
Common supported pre-crossing forecasts enter comparisons, with equal approach weight.
Missing forecasts remain visible in coverage and are never scored as zero error.
Retrospective analytical gate-crossing truth is used for scoring, not model features.
March is training/development/previously inspected exploratory data.
Protected April evaluation is separately labeled and stays fixed when controls change.
Arrival is an analytical gate proxy, not verified terminal docking.
Injected annotation labels are audience-only and never enter model features.
Guard alerts are provisional and imperfect; no calibrated operational policy or measured savings claim is implied.

replayMotion.position: Interpolate only between already delivered positions using the replay clock; the displayed vessel may trail the latest message.
replayMotion.heading: Interpolate course along the shortest angular path.
replayMotion.inference: No changes to reports, forecasts or scoring inputs.

narrative.overview:
Harbor Shift Logbook is a practical traffic console with a warm paper shell, measured sans typography, flat ruled groups, and a dark geographic chart. The identity comes from careful alignment, readable numbers, and restrained color. It has no simulated aging, decorative shoreline illustration, or ornamental motion.

The shell supports a presenter inspecting evidence. Controls, forecasts, delivered messages, and explanatory notes must remain legible together. Clear labels and source limits carry the meaning; visual status must never imply more certainty than the underlying research supports.
keyCharacteristics: Warm paper and ink surrounding a dark harbor chart.
A familiar sans family with tabular numeric readouts.
Teal action and Antidote response; separate model and annotation colors.
Flat groups divided by rules, with compact native controls.
Restrained transitions that follow user action and the replay clock.

rules.name: The Meaning Before Color Rule
rules.body: Pair every model, condition, and warning color with a code, label, symbol, or explanatory text. Red field annotations mean known simulated changes for the audience; they do not mean the model detected a fault.

rules.name: The Shared Clock Rule
rules.body: Keep time, units, and retrospective scoring labels visible beside the evidence they describe. An unavailable value is shown as an em dash or an explicit unavailable state.

rules.name: The Ruled Surface Rule
rules.body: Separate ordinary content with borders, alignment, and tonal surfaces. Reserve floating shadows for vessel labels and hulls over the map.

dos: Do preserve the warm paper, ink, and dark chart relationship.
Do keep controls native, labeled, and visibly focusable.
Do use tabular numbers for time, outputs, metrics, reports, vessel facts, and map labels.
Do preserve selected, unavailable, loading, quiet-window, review, and error states with explicit text.
Do keep explanatory footnotes attached to charts and the protected evaluation clearly separate from interactive results.
Do let narrow layouts stack the console and charts while retaining the same evidence and units.
donts: Don't add faux aged paper, illustrative geography, or decorative motion.
Don't turn every section into a raised or rounded card.
Don't use red simulated annotations as a detection-success claim or treat a clear guard state as proof that a forecast is correct.
Don't fill empty metrics with invented values or score missing forecasts as zero error.
Don't replace the coordinate fallback with an imitation basemap or omit its unavailability label.
Don't describe the analytical gate as verified docking or the March replay as protected evaluation evidence.
